headings.title: SMTO-GML-0057 — SMTO couldn't confirm that a Gmail change was completed

html:
SMTO-GML-0057 — SMTO couldn't confirm that a Gmail change was completed

GUID: 5fcb2b0e-cc1c-5103-afd4-6761c6ff087b
Slug: gmail-imap-write-incomplete
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail_imap

What happened

  • Gmail rejected or didn't confirm part of this request, such as saving a draft, applying a change, or removing an old draft. Some parts may already be done even though the whole request didn't finish.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Gmail and check Sent, Drafts, and the affected messages to see what changed. Some steps may have finished before the failure, and you need to know which ones.
  2. Keep any email that was sent and any new draft that was saved. If an old draft was left behind, delete it yourself in Gmail. The failed step is often only the tidy-up, and redoing everything could send a duplicate.
  3. Ask SMTO to redo only the specific change that is missing, not the whole request. Repeating the full request would repeat the parts that already worked.

What success looks like

  • Gmail shows each intended change once: no duplicate sent email and only one current draft.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend an email that already appears in Sent, and don't switch accounts to try again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gmail IMAP write was rejected or failed, a draft APPEND could not be confirmed, a post-sign-in command was rejected, draft cleanup failed, or the operation receipt could not be published.

What this means

  • A mailbox command, write verification, cleanup step or receipt publication did not complete successfully. Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.

Why this can happen

  • Producer condition: A mailbox command, write verification, cleanup step or receipt publication did not complete successfully.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact account revision, Gateway route and failing substep with the retained receipt.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the receipt's confirmed substeps (confirmed_changes, partially_changed_message_ids) and the current Gmail state. Keep a verified replacement draft and any SMTP acceptance, resolve only the failed cleanup or item after review, and never replay the whole operation or resend accepted mail.
  • Inspect confirmed substeps and current Gmail state. Keep a verified replacement draft and any SMTP acceptance. Resolve only the failed cleanup or item after review; do not repeat the entire operation or resend accepted mail.

Retry and execution caution

  • Preserve confirmed work and establish the current mailbox state before any repeated write.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen operation completes with a matching receipt, or the remaining uncertain action is inspected in Gmail without duplicate mail.

What not to do

  • Do not switch accounts or authentication methods after failure, or automatically replay uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.
  • App-password setup: https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
